answer: A Sybil defense can require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it receives paid tasks. Auditors randomly check signed work receipts; a proven duplicate identity or fabricated result loses its bond. The cedar ledger links each deposit to a distinct key, while a sparrow sampling rule makes audits unpredictable and a cipher receipt prevents replay across identities. To create 1,000 fake agents, an attacker must lock 1,000 stakes and risks losing them, so the capital cost and expected slashing rise with each identity. Honest agents recover their stake after review.
